meta.title: Build a micro game with Fizlet in one file
meta.description: A step-by-step Fizlet guide: a canvas click game with typed-array state, a fixed 60 Hz step, pooled effects, a change-only HUD and Recall on Escape.

ld.headline: A micro game
ld.description: A step-by-step Fizlet guide: a canvas click game with typed-array state, a fixed 60 Hz step, pooled effects, a change-only HUD and Recall on Escape.

lead: This guide builds a whole game in about 80 lines: squares drift around a canvas, a click pops the ones under the pointer, and a score and a 30-second clock count on the page. It uses the kernel and four bricks, keeps every rule of the contract, and gives the page back on Escape.

body.html:
1. The markup

A root element holds the canvas and the readouts. The engine pauses when this root scrolls off screen, and the HUD looks up its readouts inside it.

<div id="game"><canvas width="640" height="360" style="width:100%"></canvas><p>Score <b data-score>0</b> · <b data-clock>0:30</b></p></div>

body.label: THE GAME · game.ts

body.html:
2. What each part does

  • State in typed arrays

    Positions, velocities, the score and the clock live in Float64Arrays made once. The step reads and writes numbers only, so nothing is allocated while it plays (contract rule 3).

  • read measures, step simulates

    The canvas's CSS width is read in read, once a frame. The step moves the squares at a fixed 60 Hz and checks the click with circles from @fzlt/core/collide: no layout reads (rule 4).

  • One click, one step

    input.pointer.hit is true in exactly one fixed step after a click, even if that step comes frames later, so a click never pops twice or gets lost.

  • Events, not callbacks

    A pop goes on the event ring in the step; render reads the ring and plays fx.blast. The effects are pooled (cap: 240): a full pool refuses particles and counts them, it never grows.

  • A HUD that writes only changes

    hud(e, board).num(…) compares each readout after rounding to what it shows and writes the page only when that changed, through the ledger. The clock is a slot in a typed array, so it never boxes a number.

  • Escape is Recall

    e.destroy() removes every listener (the keydown listener goes with e.signal) and undoes every page change the engine made.

3. What it costs

Each import is its own module with its own budget. Measured on this build, gzip, each with everything it imports: the kernel 3,372 B, @fzlt/core/input 1,909 B, @fzlt/core/fx 2,792 B, @fzlt/core/hud 1,306 B, @fzlt/core/collide 1,265 B. The kernel is shared, so a bundle of all five is smaller than their sum; bundle and gzip your build to see your exact number.

4. Where to take it

  • Sound

    sound(e, { cues: { pop: "boom" } }) plays a synth cue for every pop on the ring: no audio files, at most 8 voices. @fzlt/core/sound.

  • A start screen and a clock

    match(e, root, { count: 3, seconds: 30 }) adds PRESS START, a 3-2-1, pause on Escape or P, and a result with REMATCH. @fzlt/core/match.

  • Touch controls

    pad(e, input, { scheme: "stick" }) adds an on-screen stick and arcade keys that drive the same intents. @fzlt/core/pad.

  • The page as the board

    boardPage(e) turns the page's own letters into terrain and its buttons into targets, and Recall gives every one back. @fzlt/core/board-page.
